content.user_title: Build Azure AI Foundry Apps with .NET
content.value_statement: .NET developers need reliable patterns for Azure AI Foundry project operations. This skill provides focused SDK guidance for agents, datasets, indexes, deployments, evaluations, connections, and authentication.
actual_capabilities: Explains package installation and Azure project endpoint configuration.
Shows authentication with DefaultAzureCredential and AIProjectClient.
Demonstrates persistent and versioned agent creation, execution, polling, and cleanup.
Covers connections, deployments, datasets, indexes, and evaluations.
Shows how to obtain Azure OpenAI chat clients from project connections.
Provides error handling, pagination, credential handling, and resource cleanup guidance.
limitations: Requires an existing Azure AI Foundry project, valid permissions, and configured model deployments.
Does not provision Azure resources or execute examples automatically.
Preview packages and APIs may differ from the documented versions.
Examples require environment-specific validation, testing, and error handling.

use_cases.title: Create a project agent
use_cases.description: Build a C# workflow that creates an agent, sends a message, polls the run, reads responses, and removes resources.

use_cases.title: Manage project data
use_cases.description: Implement dataset upload, Azure AI Search index management, and project connection discovery with the Azure SDK.

use_cases.title: Run model evaluations
use_cases.description: Configure relevance evaluators, start an evaluation, inspect status, and plan production monitoring.

prompt_templates.title: Set up the SDK
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to configure Azure.AI.Projects in a .NET application. Include required packages, environment variables, authentication, and a client initialization checklist.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new Azure AI Foundry project.

prompt_templates.title: Build a persistent agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a C# persistent agent workflow for [TASK]. Include thread creation, messages, polling, response reading, error handling, and cleanup.

prompt_templates.title: Manage project resources
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an implementation plan for managing [RESOURCE_TYPE] with Azure.AI.Projects. Cover listing, creation, versioning, deletion, pagination, and permission requirements.
prompt_templates.scenario: Add datasets, indexes, deployments, connections, or evaluations.

prompt_templates.title: Review a production integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Azure AI Projects .NET design for production readiness. Assess authentication, credential exposure, retries, polling, cleanup, versioning, observability, and preview API risks.

output_examples.input: Plan a persistent math tutor agent in C#.
output: Agent, thread, message, and run workflow.

output_examples.input: Explain how to upload and retrieve a project dataset.
output_examples.output: A concise implementation sequence covering connection selection, dataset naming, versioning, file or folder upload, retrieval, and optional deletion.

output_examples.input: Review an evaluation workflow for production.
output_examples.output: A structured review covering evaluator configuration, deployment dependencies, asynchronous execution, status checks, diagnostics, access control, and operational monitoring.

best_practices: Use DefaultAzureCredential and grant only the permissions required by the application.
Use asynchronous SDK methods, bounded polling delays, and clear timeout handling.
Delete temporary agents, threads, datasets, and indexes when the workflow no longer needs them.
anti_patterns: Do not embed credentials, connection secrets, or project endpoints in source control.
Do not request connection credentials unless the current operation requires them.
Do not copy preview examples into production without checking package versions and current API documentation.

faq.question: Which .NET packages are required?
faq.answer: Azure.AI.Projects and Azure.Identity provide the core client and authentication. Agent extensions may require preview packages.

faq.question: How does authentication work?
faq.answer: The examples use DefaultAzureCredential. It can use local developer credentials or managed identity, depending on the environment.

faq.question: Can this skill create Azure resources?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation guidance for project operations after the required Azure resources and permissions exist.

faq.question: Does it cover both persistent and versioned agents?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents persistent agent operations and versioned agents through the Azure.AI.Projects.OpenAI preview package.

faq.question: Are the examples production ready?
faq.answer: They are reference patterns. Add environment validation, retries, timeouts, observability, access controls, and tests before production use.

faq.question: Can it help with datasets and evaluations?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers dataset uploads, retrieval, deletion, evaluator configuration, evaluation creation, status retrieval, and listing.
